_comment: Generated by tools/make_egg.py from packaging/rift/install.sh: edit that and run it.
name: Rift Event Server
author: owner@nissoco.com
description: Rift Event Server: a Minecraft 26.3 server written in Rust. Installs the Linux x86-64 build from the GitHub release named by RIFT_VERSION. The prepared game files (made from your own Minecraft copy with rift-prepare) are uploaded to resources/ by hand.

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# The Pterodactyl egg's install script (packaging/rift/pterodactyl-egg.json holds a copy: tools/make_egg.py
# writes it, so edit this file and run that). It runs once in an install container with the server folder at
# /mnt/server, at install and at reinstall, and puts the Linux x86-64 build of Rift Event Server there: the
# programs in rift/, start.sh at the top. It touches no world, no settings and no game files.
#
# RIFT_VERSION  the release to install: "nightly" (every push to dev) or a tag. The egg's variable.
# RIFT_REPO     the GitHub repository the releases are in.
# The rest is for testing the script away from a panel: RIFT_BASE_URL (where releases are), RIFT_ROOT (the
# server folder) and RIFT_SKIP_APT.
set -eu

version="${RIFT_VERSION:-nightly}"
repo="${RIFT_REPO:-Nissoco23/rift-event-server}"
base="${RIFT_BASE_URL:-https://github.com/$repo/releases/download}"
root="${RIFT_ROOT:-/mnt/server}"
asset="rift-server-linux-x86_64.tar.gz"

if [ -z "${RIFT_SKIP_APT:-}" ]; then
  apt-get update -qq
  apt-get install -y -qq curl ca-certificates tar
fi

work=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT

echo "Downloading Rift Event Server ($version)..."
curl -fsSL "$base/$version/$asset" -o "$work/$asset"
curl -fsSL "$base/$version/$asset.sha256" -o "$work/$asset.sha256"

# The download is checked against the checksum published beside it.
expected=$(cut -d' ' -f1 "$work/$asset.sha256")
if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  actual=$(sha256sum "$work/$asset" | cut -d' ' -f1)
else
  actual=$(shasum -a 256 "$work/$asset" | cut -d' ' -f1)
fi
if [ -z "$expected" ] || [ "$expected" != "$actual" ]; then
  echo "The download does not match its checksum (expected '$expected', got '$actual'): nothing was installed." >&2
  exit 1
fi

mkdir -p "$root/rift" "$root/resources"
tar -xzf "$work/$asset" -C "$root"
chmod +x "$root/start.sh" "$root/rift/rift-server" "$root/rift/rift-engine"

echo "Installed. Upload the prepared game files to resources/ (docs/hosting.md, step 2), set the EULA"
echo "variable to true, and start the server."

variables.name: Rift release
variables.description: The release to install: nightly (every push to dev) or a tag. Read at install and reinstall.

variables.name: EULA
variables.description: true accepts the Minecraft EULA (https://aka.ms/MinecraftEULA). Until then the server stops at start and says why. Read on the first start.

variables.name: Online mode
variables.description: false behind a Velocity proxy that signs players in (put the proxy's forwarding.secret in the server folder). true checks players' Minecraft accounts here. Read on the first start.

variables.name: Whitelist
variables.description: true: only whitelisted players and operators can join. Read on the first start.

variables.name: Players
variables.description: Names to whitelist, separated by commas. Read on the first start.

variables.name: Operator
variables.description: A name to make an operator. Read on the first start.

variables.name: World
variables.description: The world folder's name. Read on the first start.

variables.name: Seed
variables.description: The world seed; empty is a random one. Read on the first start.

variables.name: Voice chat port
variables.description: The UDP port for voice chat (Simple Voice Chat): allocate it to the server in the panel and open it (UDP) to players. Written to config/voicechat.toml at each start.

variables.name: Voice chat host
variables.description: Leave empty behind a Velocity proxy that runs the Simple Voice Chat plugin (it bridges the voice to this server's voice port). Otherwise the server's own public address, for example voice.example.com or voice.example.com:24454; empty means the address players play on. Written to config/voicechat.toml at each start.
